rv.q: The actors bring joy and funk to spare to “Sister Act.”
This production of Sister Act has that phenomenal magic that will draw audiences back to Mercury Theater Chicago.

This is a blockbuster, folks, and recertifies the importance of the Mercury Theater Chicago, and it’s busy cabaret venue Venus, as an essential element to both the Southport Corridor and the Chicago theatrical landscape.

Carter, director Reneisha Jone'ne Jenkins, and the cast have a great time with this show, with the result that the audience, at least on opening night, was able to dive into it with lots of vocal callbacks and jubilation. The play is structured as a philosophical conflict between disco diva Deloris (Alexis J.
How did Reneisha Jenkins, making her directorial debut, work something of a miracle with her Mercury Theater production of “Sister Act”?
This production sparkles with comedy, great music, plenty of heart and, thanks to Marquecia Jordan’s array of gorgeous, glitzy, habit-forming costumes, more sequins and spangles than Cher’s closet.

But if you’re tired of the slings and arrows of stupid fate and want a sweet, silly, soulful escape with a tender beating heart at its center (contra Rudnick, these nuns really aren’t that scary), Sister Act has your balm in Gilead.
Sister Act is a fun and uplifting comedy delivered by a charismatic cast.

This delightful two hours and twenty minutes of live musical theater with music by Alan Menkin and lyrics by Glenn Slater will continue through January 2nd with performances as follows: Wednesdays 7:30 p.m.
A must see, this is a great show for a night out with family or friends.

cn.t: Critics praise this Mercury Theater production as joyous comfort food that exceeds expectations, with director Reneisha Jenkins elevating familiar material through spirited performances and high-energy staging.
